correctness.rationale: For arbitrary centered symmetric full-dimensional compact convex sections in each d>=2, global depth maximality at a slice center follows from reflection and the direct quasiconcavity argument. Steep tilted halfspaces give exact a0/2 and a2/2 outer-center depths. The middle-center mass is a1/2+a2+F0(u,t)-F2(u,t), and symmetry F_i(u,-t)=a_i-F_i(u,t) yields its infimum a1/2+a0-D. Horizontal directions cannot lower it since D>=0 and D>=a0-a2. Strict separation of points outside compact convex bodies proves D=0 iff K0 subset K2 and D=a0-a2 iff K2 subset K0. The nested >1/4 inequality follows from incompatible inequalities M<=a1+m and a1+3m<=M. In the equal-volume case, cap differences satisfy D<v/2 strictly by the common interior neighborhood and compact direction/threshold domain; crosswise thin rectangles give D->v/2 and sharp normalized infimum 1/3. originality.rationale: The full mathematical text of Cheng--Basu 2026 and two closest published published-finding corpus results were compared by logical implication. Cheng--Basu establishes a universal 2/9 lower bound under midpoint inclusion, not an exact discrepancy classification for arbitrary centered symmetric slices without midpoint inclusion. The reflected-core result exactly covers a homothetic symmetric specialization, but assumes layers (rK,K,K), hence does not cover three different incomparable symmetric bodies or the sharp crossed-rectangle one-third law. The equal-area result assumes midpoint inclusion, which forces translated identical slices; it does not cover our non-midpoint crossed-rectangle regime. Multiple actual published-finding corpus semantic queries located these as nearest hits and no dominating statement. This establishes documented best-knowledge originality, not independent historical priority.

value.rationale: The exact maximum-depth problem for three parallel convex slices is directly motivated by the recent sharp three-slice centerpoint theorem. This result characterizes an infinite all-dimensional geometrically natural symmetric class by one signed halfspace-cap invariant, proves that a depth optimizer must be a slice center, and quantitatively detects precisely when outer-slice nesting makes depth volume-only. The strict sharp 1/4 universal nested infimum and distinct sharp 1/3 equal-mass nonnested infimum (with explicit crossed-rectangle witnesses and a 1D contrast) are motivated extrema, not table lookups, arbitrary slices, or textbook deductions. Full nonnested dependence on shape makes the invariant necessary rather than decorative. This does not claim a general mixed-integer conjecture solution.
